questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a spanish speaking country, and a big city close to the water - and a city that I had never visited.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was confusing how late we had to select courses, and nobody really understood what was going on, but otherwise it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not alot. Some emails I guess. We had a meeting with the university where they explained more or less how it all works and the date of first day and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I first went to an airbnb for 20 days and from there I started to meet up with other Erasmus students and heard from them how they found housing. After 15 days I had an apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Look for a place that has heaters, because it gets really really cold in the old apartments in the wintermonths.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to research what courses at the host university would fit well with your study and then check with the host university if it made sense or if you had to change something.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: On the day I had to choose a student counsler checked it with me and helped me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not end up with the courses I had planned out, because they were spread out on two semesters, so I found some others, and it was quite difficult to get it all to make sense, but in the end I had a schedule with no overlaps.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make an appointment with the student counsler just to make sure you do it right the first time and that you got the dates right and don't waste your time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some teachers were good and others not so helpful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The exams were hard to pass even though I did study quite a lot. it was clear that some professors had higher expectations than others to the Erasmus students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My courses un literature were quite similar to the ones I've had in CPH - not the same content, but same methods of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'Financial Accounting', 'Introduction to Business Management', 'Contemporary Spanish readers', 'Literature and modernity in Latin America' and 'Norms and correct usage of Spanish'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 'Norms and correct usage of Spanish' was fun and nice to refresh some grammar and get to know the rules better while practicing the language.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: flight home for christmas, a proper duvet, trips to other cities in Spain, a bike.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is cheaper, but the culture is also to eat out more, so it's not really that much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not check it out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they had a lot of offers, I just didn't join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bike around the city, do sports in Turia park, or creative things in the park.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The beach, the museeums, the city of science.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy in the sense of the eatingtimes and such. It was not easy socialising with the locals, most of my friends are also on Erasmus.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seem open and talk spanish the best you can.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that they don't recycle clothes that much here, so many buy from big companies such as Zara, Bull & Bear and Bershka, that in my opinion is bad quality and not sustainable. It's not a big problem or anything, I just noticed that vintage clothes is not as big here as in Copenhagen, also because it's more expensive than the new clothes here.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, and the fact that the day starts a couple of hours later and that there is life on the streets at 22-23 still.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It gets cold at night, also in most apartments - have something warm to sleep in. 
don't leave your phone, wallet etc. unattended at the beach.
Use the libraries to study - there are many nice ones.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with people who only talk Spanish. Reading a lot of literature in Spanish. The friends I've made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My exam in Financial Accounting (wich is not my field normally) and my big assignments in spanish.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
